title: Prove five A2 targets need five rank-three calls (no κ)
body:
## Summary

Scoped written proof with exact finite corroboration, produced by Nick Petalas. Five identical A2 longest-element targets `w0=sts=tst` have exact formal cost `5 f(3)` at paid scalar rank cap three, over every field and with arbitrary finite restored dirty spectators. The common rank price is nonnegative, nondecreasing and discretely concave, with `f(0)=0`.

```diff
- fixed disjoint batching: 6 calls, ranks (3,3,3,2,2,2), cost 3 f(3)+3 f(2)
+ changing supports:      5 calls, ranks (3,3,3,3,3),   cost 5 f(3)
```

At `f(k)=k/(k+1)`, this is `15/4` instead of `17/4`, saving `1/2`. The new five-call support schedule attains the inherited 15-unit rank floor. It needs no scalar mixing or additional role; the lower bound still allows arbitrary scalar couplings, free scalar GL mixing and restored dirty workspace.

This answers one nondivisible-target case posed in Benny Zhao / zhaobenny's #6817. Credit #6817 for the all-field rank-cap model and lower bound, David Arias #2738 for its Coxeter predecessor, Nick Petalas #5083 for the older cap-two changing-support construction, ToikY #6821 for the distinct repeated-st tariff, and the retained Adam Gall, Ross Richardson, ywz65, eumemic, Ali Romman and Gareth Davidson lineage. The new claim is the five-target/cap-three schedule and exact tariff. Predecessor mathematical results are cited without replaying their scientific programs.

[Advance CLAIM](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19538441). The delivered scope matches it. Only `research/a2-five-target-cap-three/` is added.

## Evidence

Local CPython 3.12.15 on macOS arm64, standard library only, at head `fe77116fcf5012533e6de748ab6089790f43ac37`:

- 24 full signed formal endpoints over Q/F2/F3/F5, five/six/eight roles and two scalar gauges. Every one of 120 paid couplings has rank three and is idempotent; 78 genuinely couple productive and dirty roles, with complete scalar entrance/exit restoration.
- A separate GL2(F2) regular-action implementation checks 912 complete basis columns. Full endpoints reject all 120 call omissions and 120 label flips.
- 36 exact rational price schedules agree with the minimum of all 90 rank-count profiles of total rank 15 through 17, for 3,240 comparisons. The written cited lower bound carries the universal circuit statement; finite checks are corroboration.
- Warning-strict normal and optimized commands both print `PASS_A2_FIVE_TARGET_CAP_THREE` with identical newly generated hash-bound receipts. Each took 0.20 s in a single local timeout check. The registered replay ran both commands and printed `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE` in 0.65 s. These are timeout measurements, not a performance comparison.
- Committed bytes, modes and source-history ancestry print `PASS_RESEARCH_COMMIT_BYTES`. Source pins and package metadata pass. The staged diff and whitespace check pass, and the worktree is clean.

Reproduce from the repository root. Another installation can substitute its CPython 3.12 executable:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -W error -B research/a2-five-target-cap-three/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -O -W error -B research/a2-five-target-cap-three/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/a2-five-target-cap-three
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/a2-five-target-cap-three --check-source-history --check-modes
```

## Limitations

This is a formal group-algebra tariff, not a native supplier, new kappa or complete multiplication theorem. Scalar coupling rank is not recursive child rank. Native realization, scalar-map costs, routing, ownership, storage, precision, stock, hosting, compilation and the complete supplier invoice remain unknown. No selected-frontier change is made; all five selected framework assumptions remain. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed. Lean, Docker, the selected cold replay and predecessor scientific suites were not run. No local mathematical obligation is deferred solely to CI.

## Open next questions

- Can a native implementation supply a rank-three call at a complete subadditive price? First specify its actual data/address layout and arbitrary-input entry/exit contract, then charge scalar maps, movement, ownership, precision and restoration. No such physical contract is supplied here.
- Which other nondivisible longest-element batches attain the packed floor? Start with a support-incidence feasibility problem at one declared target count and cap. This proof gives no general scheduling theorem or chronology obstruction. No follow-on scope is reserved.

## Related open work

- [#3893](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3893) studies a mixed three-role S3 endpoint with rank-one calls. This result uses five identical longest-element targets and cap three; it computes no common optimum with that PR.

The related-work refresh also examined #7178 and #7180 through #7184. These concern shell growth, Gaussian inverse norms, Clifford sectors, cube-zero lifts, radical tariffs and rational headers. None computes this five-target/cap-three tariff. No extra scientific comparison computations were run.
